title: Beliefs & Foundations
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first basics of Islam. Covers Allah’s uniqueness and names, sincerity, repentance, patience in dua, angels, revelation, earlier scriptures, resurrection, judgment, divine decree and seeking knowledge. Uses simple meanings, familiar learning situations and short everyday choices. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on first basics through simple meanings, connections between familiar ideas and straightforward applications. No specialist theological debate or advanced terminology is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday and classroom scenarios illustrate the cited teachings. References to the Injil and Zabur concern the scriptures Allah revealed. Divine decree is presented alongside effort; patience in dua is not a promise of a requested outcome on a chosen timetable. General teachings about recording deeds and judgment do not assign adult legal accountability to young children. No question asks a child to judge another person’s faith or worth. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which statement matches the Quran's teaching about Allah and His creation?

options.text: Nothing in creation is like Allah
Allah is a larger version of a person
Allah is the same as the sun
Allah changes into different animals

questions.explanation: Allah is unlike His creation. We learn about Him from revelation rather than imagining Him as a created thing.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach us to use when calling upon Allah?

options.text: Names we invent for Him
His beautiful names
The names of our favorite toys
Only the names of places

questions.explanation: Allah's beautiful names help us learn about Him. The Quran teaches us to call upon Him by those names.

questions.question: What does Ayat al-Kursi teach about Allah and sleep?

options.text: He must sleep every night
He needs a nap after helping people
Neither sleepiness nor sleep overtakes Him
He sleeps whenever the sun sets

questions.explanation: Allah does not become sleepy or need sleep. His care for creation does not tire Him.

questions.question: What does it mean that Allah is Self-Sufficient?

options.text: He needs people to feed Him
He needs a house built by people
He depends on the weather
He does not need help from His creation

questions.explanation: Allah needs nothing from us. We depend on Him, while He does not depend on His creation.

questions.question: What does sincere worship mean?

options.text: Worshipping Allah to please Him
Worshipping only to impress people
Worshipping only to win a prize
Worshipping only when someone is watching

questions.explanation: Sincerity means directing our worship to Allah. Other people's attention should not be its purpose.

questions.question: What is tawbah?

options.text: Boasting about an unkind choice
Sincerely turning back to Allah after wrongdoing
Planning to repeat a wrong for fun
Pretending wrongdoing can never be corrected

questions.explanation: Tawbah means returning to Allah sincerely. It includes regretting wrongdoing, stopping it and intending to do better.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach us to avoid when making dua?

options.text: Calling upon Allah respectfully
Continuing to ask Allah
Impatience about the answer
Turning to Allah with hope

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned against impatience in dua. We should not give up because we have not received what we asked for yet.

questions.question: According to the Prophet ﷺ, from what were angels created?

options.text: Wood
Ice
Metal
Light

questions.explanation: An authentic hadith teaches that angels were created from light. We learn this through revelation, not by guessing.

questions.question: What task does Surah Al-Infitar describe for some angels?

options.text: Recording people's deeds
Writing made-up stories about people
Choosing winners in every game
Making people forget their names

questions.explanation: The Quran describes honorable angels who record deeds. Their task is real, not a storybook invention.

questions.question: Which angel brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by Allah's permission?

options.text: A teacher named by the class
Jibril, also called Gabriel
An unknown king
A traveler who wrote his own message

questions.explanation: Jibril brought the revelation by Allah's permission. The Quran's message came from Allah, not from the angel's own ideas.

questions.question: Which revealed scripture does the Quran say Allah gave to Isa, son of Maryam?

options.text: The Zabur
The Quran
The Injil
A book written by his classmates

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches that Allah gave Isa the Injil. It was revelation containing guidance, not a book Isa invented.

questions.question: To which prophet did Allah give the Zabur?

options.text: Nuh
Yusuf
Yunus
Dawud

questions.explanation: The Quran names Dawud as the prophet given the Zabur. Learning this helps us recognize earlier revelation.

questions.question: In which language was the Quran revealed?

options.text: Arabic
Bangla
English
Turkish

questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed in Arabic. Translations help readers understand its meanings in other languages.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in relation to revelation?

options.text: An angel who wrote his own religion
A human being who received revelation
A god who created people
A person who guessed Allah's message

questions.explanation: Muhammad ﷺ was a human messenger who received revelation. Receiving Allah's message did not make him divine.

questions.question: What does the Quran describe Allah's Messenger ﷺ as for believers?

options.text: Someone whose actions never teach us anything
Someone whose guidance is only for kings
An excellent example to follow
Someone we should ignore when learning Islam

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ is an excellent example. Learning his guidance helps us understand how to live our faith.

questions.question: Does the Quran tell us the stories of every messenger Allah sent?

options.text: Yes, every messenger's life is described
No, Allah sent only one messenger
Yes, it lists every messenger's hometown
No, some are told and others are not

questions.explanation: Allah tells us about some messengers and not others. We should not invent details about those not described.

questions.question: What does resurrection mean in Islamic belief?

options.text: Being raised to life again after death
Turning into a different animal each year
Sleeping for a few hours
Remembering an old school day

questions.explanation: Resurrection means being raised after death. The Quran teaches that people will be raised on the Day of Judgment.

questions.question: What does the Quran say will be presented on the Day of Judgment?

options.text: Only a list of favorite meals
The record of deeds
Only the names of popular people
A record that Allah cannot understand

questions.explanation: The Quran describes the record of deeds being presented. Allah's judgment is fair and wrongs no one.

questions.question: Belief in qadar means believing in what?

options.text: The power of lucky numbers
The idea that Allah knows nothing beforehand
Allah's divine decree
The idea that events are beyond Allah's control

questions.explanation: Qadar means Allah's divine decree. The Prophet ﷺ included belief in it among the foundations of faith.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach us to ask Allah to increase?

options.text: Our desire to boast
Our ability to mock others
Our habit of ignoring lessons
Our knowledge

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches a prayer for more knowledge. Learning is something we can seek Allah's help with.

questions.question: Why should we avoid describing Allah as a giant human?

options.text: Allah is unlike anything He created
All humans eventually become gods
Allah is only a character in a picture
A taller person is always more divine

questions.explanation: The Creator is not a larger version of His creatures. The Quran teaches that nothing is like Him.

questions.question: Why is learning Allah's beautiful names useful?

options.text: They let us invent anything about Allah
They teach us about Allah and help us make dua
They replace every other kind of learning
They are only a spelling competition

questions.explanation: Learning Allah's names is more than memorizing sounds. Their meanings help us know Him and call upon Him.

questions.question: When people are asleep, does Allah's care for creation stop?

options.text: Yes, everyone must wait until morning
Yes, creation looks after Allah at night
No, Allah does not sleep or become tired
No, because another god takes His place

questions.explanation: Allah is always sustaining His creation. Unlike people, He does not need rest or someone to take over.

questions.question: Does Allah need our worship to become stronger?

options.text: Yes, each prayer gives Him more strength
Yes, without people He cannot exist
No, but He needs food instead
No, Allah does not depend on us

questions.explanation: Our worship does not supply Allah with something He lacks. He is Self-Sufficient, and we are the ones who need Him.

questions.question: If nobody notices our worship, can we still worship sincerely?

options.text: Yes, pleasing Allah is what matters
No, worship counts only when friends notice
No, praise from people is its only purpose
Yes, but only if we complain afterward

questions.explanation: Sincerity is about why we worship Allah. An audience is not required for sincere devotion.

questions.question: Which choice best matches sincere tawbah?

options.text: Say sorry while planning the same wrong for fun
Regret the wrong and honestly try to stop it
Blame everyone else without reflecting
Claim that changing our behavior never matters

questions.explanation: Tawbah is a sincere return to Allah, not just words. We should turn away from wrongdoing and try to improve.

questions.question: If a request is not fulfilled immediately, what should we remember about dua?

options.text: Allah must follow our chosen timetable
We should stop every dua forever
We should remain patient when calling upon Allah
Only requests answered in one minute matter

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught patience in dua. A delay is not a reason to declare that making dua is useless.

questions.question: How do we know that angels were created from light?

options.text: We can learn it by drawing a cartoon
Every bright lamp contains an angel
We can discover it from a guessing game
The Prophet ﷺ taught it in an authentic hadith

questions.explanation: This knowledge comes from an authentic report from the Prophet ﷺ. Pictures and guesses do not establish facts about angels.

questions.question: Are the angels who record deeds just imaginary story characters?

options.text: No, they are real angels described in the Quran
Yes, they exist only in cartoons
Yes, people invented them for games
No, they are actually schoolteachers

questions.explanation: Belief in recording angels comes from the Quran. Their existence does not depend on whether we can see them.

questions.question: Did Jibril invent the Quran's message before delivering it?

options.text: Yes, he made it up for entertainment
No, he brought revelation by Allah's permission
Yes, he copied a classroom story
No, a king invented it instead

questions.explanation: Jibril conveyed Allah's revelation. Delivering the message did not make him its author.

questions.question: Does believing in the Quran mean denying that Allah gave Isa a revealed scripture?

options.text: Yes, Isa received no guidance from Allah
Yes, only Muhammad ﷺ ever received revelation
No, the Quran itself affirms that gift
No, but the Injil was given to Dawud

questions.explanation: The Quran affirms that Allah gave Isa the Injil. Believing in earlier revelation is part of learning Islam's foundations.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a prophet with the scripture Allah gave him?

options.text: Dawud and the Quran
Yusuf and the Injil
Nuh and the Zabur
Dawud and the Zabur

questions.explanation: The Quran specifically links Dawud with the Zabur. Keeping the names together helps us remember the correct relationship.

questions.question: Does reading a Bangla explanation change the Quran's original language?

options.text: No, the Quran was revealed in Arabic
Yes, its original language changes with each reader
Yes, Arabic is only a later translation
No, it was originally in English

questions.explanation: An explanation or translation can help us understand. It does not change the language in which the Quran was revealed.

questions.question: Does being Allah's messenger make Muhammad ﷺ a god?

options.text: Yes, every messenger is a separate god
No, he was a human who received revelation
Yes, receiving guidance makes anyone divine
No, because he never received revelation

questions.explanation: Prophets receive revelation from Allah, but they are not gods. Muhammad ﷺ taught that God is One.

questions.question: What does following the Prophet's ﷺ example involve?

options.text: Learning his name but ignoring all his guidance
Following whatever a popular person invents
Learning his guidance and trying to act on it
Assuming his example has nothing to teach us

questions.explanation: An example guides behavior. We learn about the Prophet ﷺ so his guidance can shape our choices.

questions.question: If we have not learned a messenger's name, does that prove Allah never sent him?

options.text: Yes, we already know every messenger's name
Yes, only names in our textbook can be real
No, because we may invent any name we like
No, some messengers are not described to us

questions.explanation: Our knowledge of messengers is not complete. The Quran says some were described to the Prophet ﷺ and some were not.

questions.question: Is resurrection the same as waking up for school tomorrow?

options.text: No, it means being raised after death
Yes, every morning is the Day of Judgment
Yes, it means changing our alarm clock
No, it means forgetting everything we learned

questions.explanation: Waking from ordinary sleep is different from resurrection. The Quran speaks of being raised after death on the Day of Judgment.

questions.question: What does the record of deeds teach us about Allah's judgment?

options.text: Only famous people's actions matter
Our actions matter, and Allah wrongs no one
Allah judges by guessing what happened
People can hide every action by forgetting it

questions.explanation: The record concerns what people did. The Quran also makes clear that Allah does not treat anyone unjustly.

questions.question: Does belief in Allah's decree mean we should stop trying to do useful things?

options.text: Yes, learning and practice are always pointless
Yes, we should refuse all useful help
No, we should still make an effort and seek help
No, because Allah's decree is not part of faith

questions.explanation: Belief in qadar goes with effort. The Prophet ﷺ taught seeking what benefits us and asking Allah for help.

questions.question: What attitude fits asking Allah for more knowledge?

options.text: Pretending we already know everything
Refusing to listen to explanations
Treating every question as shameful
Being willing to learn more

questions.explanation: Asking for knowledge recognizes that we can keep learning. We can turn to Allah while making an honest effort to understand.

questions.question: Someone says, "Allah is just like a very big person." Which response fits the Quran?

options.text: Allah is unlike His creation
Allah is only slightly taller than people
Allah looks like whichever person we choose
Allah is a person who became powerful

questions.explanation: We should not describe Allah as a giant person. The Quran teaches that nothing is like Him.

questions.question: Aminah learns one of Allah's beautiful names. What is a good next step?

options.text: Make up a different name for Allah
Learn its meaning and use it respectfully in dua
Treat it as a nickname for a toy
Decide that its meaning never matters

questions.explanation: Learning the meaning helps us understand what we are saying. Allah's beautiful names should be used with respect.

questions.question: Yusuf wonders whether Allah must rest while the family sleeps. Which answer fits Ayat al-Kursi?

options.text: Allah sleeps only when all people sleep
Allah needs the family to wake Him
Allah needs neither sleep nor rest
Allah stops caring for creation every night

questions.explanation: People need sleep, but Allah does not. Caring for the heavens and earth does not tire Him.

questions.question: A classmate says, "Allah needs us to bring Him food." What should you explain?

options.text: Allah needs only our favorite food
Allah needs more food than a whole city
Allah can only eat when someone helps Him
Allah is Self-Sufficient and needs no food from us

questions.explanation: Allah does not depend on His creation. People need His provision; He does not need us to provide for Him.

questions.question: Maryam notices she is reciting only to collect compliments. What is a better intention?

options.text: Recite to worship and please Allah
Recite only to make classmates jealous
Recite only when a prize is promised
Recite to prove nobody else matters

questions.explanation: We can renew our intention and focus on Allah. Sincere worship is not about collecting attention from other people.

questions.question: Ali regrets deliberately being unkind. Which plan shows sincere turning back to Allah?

options.text: Say sorry but plan more unkindness for fun
Ask Allah's forgiveness and work on stopping the behavior
Boast that changing is unnecessary
Refuse to think about doing better

questions.explanation: A sincere return includes regret and an effort to stop the wrong. Ali can ask a trusted adult for help improving his behavior.

questions.question: Zaynab made dua but has not received what she requested. What is a good response?

options.text: Decide dua is useless after one try
Demand that Allah follow her deadline
Keep turning to Allah patiently
Mock anyone who keeps making dua

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned against impatience in dua. Zaynab can keep asking with hope without setting a deadline for Allah.

questions.question: A video claims angels are made of ice. Which source should a lesson follow?

options.text: The video because it has colorful effects
A guess from the comments
Whichever answer gets the most laughs
The authentic hadith saying angels were created from light

questions.explanation: Reliable religious learning relies on authentic evidence. The hadith about angels' creation teaches that they were created from light.

questions.question: Hasan reads about honorable angels recording deeds. Which sentence belongs in his notes?

options.text: The Quran teaches that angels record deeds
Angels are only characters in a guessing game
The Quran says no angels have tasks
Recording angels are ordinary people with wings

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Infitar describes honorable recording angels. We should learn what revelation teaches rather than inventing details.

questions.question: A lesson has three cards: Allah, Jibril and Muhammad ﷺ. Which sentence correctly connects them?

options.text: Muhammad ﷺ invented a message for Jibril
Jibril conveyed Allah's revelation to Muhammad ﷺ
Jibril created Allah before sending a book
A king gave Allah a classroom story

questions.explanation: The message was Allah's revelation. Jibril brought it to the Prophet ﷺ by Allah's permission.

questions.question: Sara is matching Isa with a scripture in her Islamic studies lesson. Which card should she choose?

options.text: The Zabur
The Quran
The Injil
A modern school workbook

questions.explanation: The Quran states that Allah gave Isa the Injil. This question concerns that revealed gift, not every book currently bearing a similar name.

questions.question: A worksheet says, "Allah gave Dawud the ____." Which word completes it?

options.text: Quran
Injil
Dictionary
Zabur

questions.explanation: The correct match is Dawud and the Zabur. This relationship is stated in the Quran.

questions.question: Adam sees Arabic verses beside English meanings. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The Arabic is the Quran; English helps explain its meanings
The Quran was first revealed in English
The English changes the original language of revelation
The Arabic was invented by the translator

questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed in Arabic. A translation offers an explanation of its meanings for readers of another language.

questions.question: A quiz card says, "Muhammad ﷺ was a human messenger who received revelation." Is it correct?

options.text: No, he was a separate god
Yes, this matches the Quran's description
No, no revelation came to him
No, every messenger must be an angel

questions.explanation: The Quran describes Muhammad ﷺ as a human receiving revelation. We honor him as Allah's messenger, not as a god.

questions.question: Fatimah learns how the Prophet ﷺ showed patience. What makes the lesson useful in her life?

options.text: Using the story only to boast about knowing facts
Deciding his example never applies to anyone else
Trying to follow that guidance in her own choices
Ignoring the lesson whenever she feels upset

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ is an example to learn from. A lesson can help us practice better conduct in familiar situations.

questions.question: A friend says their short storybook includes every messenger Allah ever sent. What is a careful reply?

options.text: A short storybook must know every messenger
Only messengers in that book ever existed
We should invent more stories to make it complete
We have not been told the stories of every messenger

questions.explanation: Allah has not told us the stories of every messenger. A short collection cannot be treated as a complete account of them all.

questions.question: A classroom poster defines resurrection. Which sentence should it use?

options.text: People will be raised after death on the Day of Judgment
People become new animals every school year
People only wake from an afternoon nap
People can choose never to face life after death

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches resurrection after death. It is part of belief in the Hereafter, not an ordinary daily waking.

questions.question: A lesson asks whether Allah's judgment depends on popularity. Which answer fits the Quran?

options.text: Yes, the most popular person always avoids judgment
No, Allah judges fairly and the deeds are recorded
Yes, only people with many friends have deeds
No, because Allah never considers what people do

questions.explanation: Popularity is not the basis of Allah's judgment. The Quran describes the record of deeds and says Allah wrongs no one.

questions.question: A game did not go as Yusuf hoped. Which response fits belief in Allah's decree?

options.text: Claim that nothing is under Allah's control
Stop all learning because effort can never matter
Accept the result, learn and keep making useful effort
Say a lucky number controls every result

questions.explanation: Belief in Allah's decree does not require giving up. Yusuf can accept a disappointment, learn from it and keep trying with Allah's help.

questions.question: Before learning a new topic, which dua meaning fits the Quran's teaching?

options.text: My Lord, make me boast about knowing everything
My Lord, help me mock people who ask questions
My Lord, make me refuse every lesson
My Lord, increase me in knowledge

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us to ask Allah for more knowledge. We can make this dua while taking part in learning.
